newsitem.title: USA: A.G. Edwards quarterly earnings fall from record levels.
newsitem.headline: A.G. Edwards quarterly earnings fall from record levels.

text.p: Brokerage A.G. Edwards Inc. said Tuesday its first-quarter earnings fell slightly from record levels a year ago, even though revenues rose as business remained strong.

The St. Louis-based financial services company earned $54.5 million, or 83 cents a share, in the quarter ended May 31 vs. $56.4 million, or 87 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues grew to $439.3 million from $428.5 million.
"Business continues good, but last year's record pace will continue to provide us with tough comparisons," Chairman Benjamin Edwards III said in a statement.
"Our first quarter of fiscal 1998 was our third best ever. However, net earnings were lower than last year's first quarter and both revenues and net earnings declined from our previous quarter."
In fiscal 1997 ended Feb. 28, A.G. Edwards earned $3.36 a share on revenues of $1.7 billion.
The company's flagship subsidiary, A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc., operates 573 brokerage offices from coast to coast.
A.G. Edwards stock was unchanged at $39 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
